title: Quota boundary entropy and drift correction for reserved & rolling windows
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:

We frequently observe small but persistent differences between what the quota controller believes a tenant has consumed and what the accounting/charge ledger records. These divergences (drift) manifest after:
- delayed or reordered usage events (edge devices / on-prem collectors),
- mid-epoch reserved capacity swaps (tenant moves between hosted -> dedicated pools),
- clock skew between ingesting services and the quota enforcer, and
- partial retries for streaming/long-running requests where per-token increments were applied out-of-band.

Problem statement:

Current reset and reconciliation behavior (daily/monthly resets and rolling-window leases) can either double-charge or under-count when events replay or arrive late relative to epoch boundaries. For reserved capacity customers, drift can cause tokens to appear consumed in the quota service while the reserved allocator still thinks there is capacity, leading to silent throttles or unexpected overage charges. Existing fixes (ad hoc backfills and manual reconciliations) are labor-intensive and not deterministic.

Goal:

Design and implement an automated drift-correction mechanism that:
1) Prevents double-counting across resets and rolling windows,
2) Provides deterministic, idempotent reset semantics even with out-of-order or delayed events,
3) Minimizes customer-visible disruption for reserved capacity and burst buckets, and
4) Produces an auditable compensating transaction when correction is necessary.

Design proposal (high level):

1) Event-sourced consumption ledger: persist every quota-affecting event as an append-only journal entry with: tenant_id, usage_units, event_ts, ingest_ts, origin_service, event_id (UUID), and epoch_tag. The epoch_tag is the quota epoch the emitter believed it was using (daily/monthly/rolling token window id).

2) Epoch watermarks and idempotent reset tokens: Introduce an epoch watermark service that issues a monotonic reset_token per tenant per epoch boundary (string token with issuance_ts). Consumers include the last_seen_reset_token with usage events. On reset, the quota enforcer compares event.reset_token to the currently active token; mismatches mean the event belongs to a previous epoch and needs to be reconciled rather than applied to the new epoch's counter. Reset tokens make resets idempotent across retries and replay.

3) Reconciliation worker (correction pass): Nightly (and on-demand) reconciliation runs that:
   a) scans the ledger for events whose ingest_ts < epoch_cutoff but applied_to_counter != true,
   b) computes per-tenant deltas between ledger-sum and counter-sum for each epoch,
   c) emits a compensating correction entry (positive or negative) with clear audit fields and a correction_reason (e.g., LATE_ARRIVAL, REPLAY_DETECTION, EPOCH_MISMATCH), and
   d) marks the ledger entries as reconciled.

4) Compensating transactions and billing-safe semantics: Corrections must not produce customer-facing invoice differences without review. For billing-impacting corrections we create a non-billing compensation record and include it in a daily audit report; Finance can configure auto-apply after a 72h review window for corrections below a threshold. Corrections that would move a tenant over a reserved-capacity commit trigger an alert for manual review.

5) Streaming & reserved capacity handling: For streaming requests that update usage mid-request (per-token), the SDK and gateway will include a transient provisional flag and a local provisional counter; final confirmation includes event_id and last_seen_reset_token so the ledger can resolve provisional increments without double-applying. Reserved capacity allocator will consult ledger watermark instead of in-memory counters for boundary decisions during rollout windows.

6) Safe rollouts and feature gates: Implement behind a feature flag per-tenant. Start with a small set of tenants (internal + pilot customers) and validate reconciliation run outputs and audit trails before ramping.

Edge cases considered:
- Replayed events with identical event_id must be idempotent and ignored on second apply.
- Long-delayed events that arrive after multiple epoch boundaries must be reconciled against the epoch they originated in, never the current epoch.
- Tenant timezone and custom billing day offsets handled by computing epoch_cutoff in tenant-local time and normalizing to UTC in the ledger.

Operational observability:
- New dashboards: per-tenant drift delta over time, number of compensating corrections, top correction reasons, and projected revenue delta.
- Alerts: per-tenant drift > 0.5% of monthly commit or > 10k tokens triggers a PagerDuty incident.

Migration plan:
1) Implement append-only ledger schema and epoch watermark service.
2) Launch reconciliation worker in dry-run mode for 7 days for pilot tenants (produces correction records but does not apply).
3) Review audits and adjust thresholds.
4) Enable auto-apply for low-risk corrections and expand rollout.
5) Deprecate existing ad hoc backfill scripts and add a final migration job to reconcile historical windows.

Why this is different from previous tickets:
This approach focuses on designing an idempotent, epoch-aware ledger + compensating correction flow rather than ad hoc resets or naive window alignment. It prioritizes auditability and billing safety for reserved capacity customers where money and SLAs are at stake.
acceptance_criteria: Append-only ledger implemented and integrated with quota enforcer for pilot tenants
Epoch watermark/reset_token service issues monotonic tokens and clients include tokens in usage events
Reconciliation worker produces compensating corrections in dry-run for pilot tenants with no applied billing changes
Dashboards surface per-tenant drift and top correction reasons
Integration tests cover replayed events, out-of-order delivery, and timezone-shifted epoch boundaries
No customer sees an unjustified quota enforcement or charge during pilot period (0 validated complaints from pilot tenants)
comments: 2025-02-18 — Maya Chen: Spiked an appendix: append-only ledger schema v1 and a PoC recon worker that computes ledger_sum vs counter_sum for 50 tenants. Observed ~0.03% monthly drift concentrated on long-tail on-prem collectors.

2025-02-20 — Design review: PM + Infra + Finance: agreed on compensating non-billing records and a 72h review window for billing-impacting corrections. Finance requested an audit CSV export schema. Action: add CSV export and finance-approval webhook.

2025-02-22 — Liam Patel: Found race where gateway reorders events under heavy load (ingest_ts < event_ts). Solution: gateway to stamp ingest_ts and forward event_id; reconciliation uses ingest_ts to decide epoch assignment.
2025-02-25 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4721 (ledger schema + epoch service). Linking once CI passes.

2025-02-28 — QA: Running reconciliation dry-run against last 30 days for 10 pilot tenants. Discovered 3 cases where reserved capacity commit would have been breached if corrections had been applied; flagged for manual review.
